quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Press the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, slow down by lifting your foot off the accelerator. Do not use the brakes until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: You are already in the intersection when the green light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Continue and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, drive through and leave the intersection as quickly as you can.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop. A passenger car going 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slower in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive so slowly that you block normal traffic flow, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has curves or turns.
There is more traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers the road is slippery when wet and they should reduce speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
There is roadwork or maintenance ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork or maintenance ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction and maintenance areas. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Traffic fines may be doubled in these areas.

questions.question: A tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the accelerator and do not brake. Let the car slow down on its own. Brake gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep the same speed.
Reduce your speed.
Move to the shoulder when it starts to rain.

questions.explanation: Slow down in rain to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast can make your tires ride on water instead of the road, causing you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
You cannot turn until the light turns green.
You may turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to watch for bicycles and other hazards that may cross the road.

questions.question: What should you do if you see animals near the road?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move or run into traffic. More animals may be hiding out of sight.

questions.question: How can you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Frequently check your rearview mirror.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to see where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: If you are 16 or 17 and are convicted of speeding more than 20 mph over the limit, how long will your license be suspended?

options.text: 30 days.
45 days.
60 days.

questions.explanation: A first offense for speeding 20 mph or more over the limit results in a 60-day license suspension for drivers age 16 or 17. You must also pay a restoration fee and court fines. Penalties increase for repeat offenses.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
Always maintain your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
questions.explanation: When you can, make room to let other vehicles merge safely into your lane.

questions.question: What should you do if you become drowsy while driving?

options.text: Try to fight it.
Take a break.
Take some caffeine pills.

questions.explanation: Stop at a rest area or service station to take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe substitute for rest.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Brake hard.
Maintain a constant speed.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: Keep the same speed when being passed. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle safely merge back into your lane.

questions.question: How can you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. Look over your shoulders to check blind spots.

questions.question: What happens when you slow down to look at collisions or unusual events?

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.explanation: Avoid slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events. This "rubbernecking" creates traffic jams.

questions.question: When driving near a distracted driver, what is the safe following distance you should keep?

options.text: One to two seconds.
Two to three seconds.
Three to four seconds.

questions.explanation: Keep at least three to four seconds of distance behind a distracted driver. Be careful when passing them. They may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?

options.text: They only affect large vehicles.
They only cause visibility problems.
They can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind reduces visibility by blowing dust and dirt onto the road. It can also physically push your vehicle.

questions.question: When should you be most careful when turning or stopping in rain?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with rain to make the road very slippery.

questions.question: Which one is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in fog.
Staring only at the road ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware of hazards. Do not stare only at the road ahead—this is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: Which factor affects how your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.explanation: Weight, biological sex, how much food you have eaten, and how many drinks you have had all affect how your body absorbs alcohol. Only time removes alcohol from your system.
